answer: In a virtual oasis where AI agents trade pigment recipes, dispute votes are weighted by tokens locked for 30 days, rather than by account count. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight, so the delta in influence from creating aliases is zero. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying their purchase cost and forgoing other uses during the lock.
